text:
For every smooth, rapidly decaying, divergence-free initial velocity on \(\R^3\) and every viscosity \(\nu>0\), we prove that the datum-generated whole-terminal compatible-rectangle theorem forces the corresponding pressure-normalized classical Navier--Stokes history to exist smoothly for all time.
The argument follows this one maximal history, with velocity and normalized pressure kept as one coupled object.
Its starting input is the whole-terminal compatible-rectangle theorem, stated here as \Cref{thm:WholeTerminalCompatibleRectangleProducer}.
For each finite temporal depth \(N\) and spatial depth \(M\), it gives one bound uniform over all cutoffs \(T<T_*\), with constants allowed to depend on \(N\) and \(M\), and makes the finite records agree under restriction.
Their projective intersection places the same velocity in every finite mixed Sobolev row.
The complete spatial row and the momentum equation give \(u_t\in L^1(I_*;H^m)\) for every finite \(m\), and hence one common endpoint \(u_*\in\bigcap_{m=0}^{\infty}H^m(\R^3)\).
The normalized pressure and velocity recurrences identify the complete endpoint jet.
Local well-posedness from \(u_*\), together with uniqueness, extends the same history past any alleged finite \(T_*\).
Consequently, the cited producer theorem together with the closure proved here makes finite maximality impossible: \(T_*=\infty\), and the normalized velocity and pressure are smooth on every finite time interval.
